title: The Case for a Trump-Xi-Putin Summit
gist: Charles Kupchan argues Trump should join a possible Trump-Xi-Putin summit at APEC in Shenzhen, aiming low on the Korean Peninsula (backing Lee Jae-myung's freeze-first plan), Ukraine de-escalation via Xi's leverage over Putin, using China's oil-import exposure to get Xi's help ending the US war in Iran, and starting trilateral arms control after New START's expiry, while not selling out Ukraine or Taiwan.

themes.theme: Trilateral summit as precedent, not a new Yalta

insights.claim: A three-way Trump-Xi-Putin summit could take place on the sidelines of the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, after Putin floated a trialogue on ending the Ukraine war, per The Wall Street Journal; no US president has ever held a trilateral meeting with Chinese and Russian leaders.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Event risk: summit headlines could move oil, Ukraine-related assets and defense stocks.
insights.quote: No U.S. president has ever held a trilateral meeting with the leaders of China and Russia

insights.claim: Charles Kupchan argues Trump would be right to join a summit with Xi and Putin even if it yields no concrete results, because it would break the ice, normalize great-power dialogue and widen the diplomatic Overton window for successors.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: A contrarian pro-engagement view from a mainstream scholar; lowers the bar for 'success'.
insights.quote: Trump is widening the diplomatic Overton window
insights.locator: Yet even though Trump, Xi, and Putin

insights.claim: Kupchan's framework holds that a global concert of great powers, modeled on the Concert of Europe, is the best way to curb rivalry in a multipolar world, but concerts only work when members accept the territorial status quo, so the time is not yet right given Russia's invasion of Ukraine and China's backing of it.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: No durable great-power settlement soon; expect rivalry to persist.
insights.quote: But the time has not come for a global concert.

insights.claim: Kupchan warns Trump, after a historic rebuke in the midterm elections two weeks before APEC, may be tempted to make concessions to Beijing and Moscow for a foreign policy win, including a closed-door Ukraine deal or softening on Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Key downside risk for Ukraine/Taiwan: watch summit readouts for concessions.
insights.quote: dealt Trump and his party a historic rebuke in the U.S. midterm elections

insights.claim: The Korean Peninsula is the best opportunity for trilateral cooperation: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung proposed replacing the 1953 armistice with a 'peace regime' and a phased denuclearization starting with a freeze on North Korean weapons development.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: A freeze deal would lower Korea risk premium.
insights.quote: jointly supporting a freeze on North Korean nuclear weapons development is a good place to start

insights.claim: Trump recently struck a deal with Putin to get more Russian diesel into global markets and waived a new round of congressional sanctions on Moscow, suggesting he cares more about lowering fuel prices than curbing Russia's war funding.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: More Russian diesel supply is bearish for diesel cracks; signals US sanctions-relaxation bias toward Russian energy.
insights.quote: struck a deal with Putin to get more Russian diesel into global markets

insights.claim: Xi has enormous leverage over Putin because China backs the Kremlin diplomatically, is the largest buyer of Russian oil and gas, and is the main supplier of dual-use semiconductors and machine tools for Russian weapons.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Any Ukraine de-escalation path runs through Beijing.
insights.quote: is the largest buyer of Russian oil and gas
insights.locator: A summit offers Trump the opportunity

insights.claim: Ukrainian drone strikes are taking a significant toll on Russia's oil sector and logistics, causing gas and commodity shortages, while some 35,000 Russian soldiers per month are killed or severely injured, pressuring Putin toward an unpopular mobilization.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Russian refining disruption supports product prices; mounting costs raise odds of a diplomatic off-ramp.
insights.quote: some 35,000 Russian soldiers per month are losing their lives or sustaining severe injuries

insights.claim: Kupchan proposes a US- and China-brokered and monitored Russia-Ukraine agreement to end attacks on energy installations, infrastructure, civilian targets and commercial shipping.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: An energy-infrastructure truce would reduce supply risk for Russian refined products and Black Sea shipping.
insights.quote: to end attacks on energy installations and infrastructure, civilian targets, and commercial shipping
insights.locator: Trump and Xi could press Putin

insights.claim: The US war in Iran is a quagmire disrupting shipping through the straits of Hormuz and Bab el Mandeb and causing soaring oil prices, and Trump needs an exit.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Oil price risk premium is tied to the Iran war; a China-brokered exit would be bearish oil.
insights.quote: disrupts shipping through the straits of Hormuz and Bab el Mandeb

insights.claim: Russia benefits from war-driven oil price spikes so is unlikely to stop supporting Iran, but China, as the largest oil importer whose large oil reserves are now significantly depleted and whose crude imports are climbing again, has an interest in ending the war.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: China's depleted strategic stocks and rising imports add to oil demand; Beijing is the swing actor for Iran de-escalation.
insights.quote: those reserves have been significantly depleted

insights.claim: China is still buying Iranian oil and supplying military intelligence and dual-use items for Iranian drones and missiles, while Russia provides satellite targeting data, munitions, drone technology and logistics.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Secondary-sanctions risk on Chinese buyers of Iranian crude.

insights.claim: Kupchan suggests Xi could press Iran to drop demands that the US withdraw Gulf forces, release frozen assets and lift sanctions, with US economic relief reserved for postwar nuclear negotiations.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Sanctions relief on Iran is a later-stage possibility, not near-term.

themes.theme: Nuclear arms control after New START

insights.claim: Every US-Russia arms control agreement has expired, with New START ending in February 2026, leaving no caps, inspections, data exchanges or exercise notifications on US and Russian strategic arsenals.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Structural tailwind for nuclear modernization spending and defense contractors.
insights.quote: This nuclear free-for-all is particularly dangerous

insights.claim: The Pentagon projects China will have more than 1,000 operational warheads by 2030, close to the roughly 1,800 operational warheads each held by the US and Russia.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Tripolar nuclear competition argues for sustained arms-race spending.
insights.quote: China will possess more than 1,000 operational warheads by 2030

insights.claim: Kupchan argues Trump can do little more than start a trilateral arms control conversation, handing it to expert teams to cover stockpile caps, military-to-military contacts, crisis protocols and exercise notifications.
insights.speaker: Charles Kupchan
insights.so_what: Do not expect binding arms control soon.
